title: Policy Composer UX — Quiet Hours & Incident Mapping (sketches)
content:
Overview:

Brainstorm + early wireframes for a single Policy Composer flow that unifies: channel fanout, severity mapping, threshold presets tied to SLOs, quiet-hours overrides, and incident mapping (which incident types create Pager/OM notifications vs only Slack threads). Goal is a single page composer that product and SRE can iterate on — low-friction defaults for PLG users, and advanced mode for enterprise customers.

Why this matters:
- Current alerts UI is fragmented: thresholds in metrics view, channels in a different modal, and quiet-hours buried under team settings. Confusing for non-SRE users.
- We need clear defaults so most users can "create alert" in < 2 minutes with safe presets (avoid pager spam).
- Enterprise customers expect fine-grained control: region-based routing, encryption of escalation channels, explicit incident types.

High-level UX goals:
1) Compose -> Preview -> Simulate -> Save
2) Surface SLO-linked presets (e.g., latency_p95 > 500ms => severity=high)
3) Allow quick toggles for Quiet Hours and Throttle windows (per-channel)
4) Provide a lightweight simulator (run on historical trace) and a message preview panel
5) Mapping table for incident types -> actions (pager / email / slack / webhook)
6) Audit-ready configuration summary (one-line export for customers)

Wireframe notes (left-to-right panes):
- Left rail: selector for the monitored object (service, model-version, route). Autocomplete and recent targets.
- Middle primary area: "Trigger" card (metric or log or anomaly).
    * Metric: choose metric (latency, error_rate, token_throttle), aggregation (p95, moving_avg), window (1m/5m/1h), comparator and value.
    * SLO tie-in: optional dropdown to "Attach to SLO" — selecting auto-populates recommended thresholds with a confidence slider (why these values).
- Right rail: "Actions & Channels"
    * Channel list with priority ordering. Each row: channel icon (Slack, PagerDuty, Email, Webhook), per-channel toggle, override options (quiet hours, rate limit, max incidents/day).
    * Inline "Throttle" slider: 0-100% for dedupe suppression; small CTA: "Recommended: 10% for high-frequency routes"
    * Per-channel quiet hours: timepicker or rule (e.g., "US-PST business hours only")
- Bottom: "Incident Mapping" panel (collapsible) with a table: Incident type | Severity | Escalation policy | On-call schedule | Auto-ack behavior | Notes

Behaviors / Edge cases:
- If user toggles "Attach to SLO" and then changes the threshold manually, show a dimmed badge: "manual override (was suggested by SLO)"
- Quiet hours should not silence critical incidents unless user explicitly checks "Allow Pager during quiet hours". Require an extra confirmation for that (modal with reminders).
- If multiple channels are configured and the first channel fails (webhook returns 5xx), automatically retry and escalate to the next channel after backoff. UI should show the fallback chain (visual timeline in the preview).

Simulator & Preview:
- Simulator button runs the rule over the last 7 days of anonymized metrics and returns: number of triggered events, estimated pages (after throttles), sample Slack message, sample PD incident.
- Also adds a cost estimate: approx pages/month and notification egress cost to help customers reason about unit economics.
- Allow uploading a small CSV of historical values for private deployments.

Backlog grooming (initial tickets and ACs):
- RDW-2789: Policy Composer MVP backend + schema (priority: P0)
  - ACs: composer API supports triggers (metric/log/anomaly), actions list, quiet_hours object, incident_mapping table; validation returns safety warnings; user can save and version.
- RDW-2812: Quiet Hours UI patterns (priority: P1)
  - ACs: per-channel quiet hours UI; timezone-aware; enterprise setting to force quiet hours for non-critical channels.
- RDW-2834: SLO-presets and confidence slider (priority: P1)
  - ACs: attaching SLO populates suggested thresholds; allow manual override; show impact estimate (simulator).
- RDW-2850: Simulator service and message preview (priority: P1)
  - ACs: run simulation against last 7 days; produce sample messages; cost estimate; accessible for hosted and private (CSV upload).
- RDW-2865: Incident mapping table & escalation preview (priority: P2)
  - ACs: CRUD on incident mappings; visual escalation chain; exportable summary for audits.

Design details / copy suggestions (short):
- Primary CTA: "Simulate & Preview" (secondary: "Save Draft")
- Warning copy for quiet-hours overrides: "Allowing pager during quiet hours will notify on-call immediately — confirm you want to enable this for severity=critical."
- Suggested presets label: "Recommended (SLO-aligned)" with tooltip: "Values based on recent traffic and SLO target — adjust if your service has known bursts."

Open questions / items for the next sync:
- How do we represent multi-region routing? (per-channel region filter vs. per-policy region) — @Ethan to propose data model.
- Throttles: do we expose token-bucket style or simple rate-per-minute? Keep simple for MVP.
- Where does team on-call schedule live? Integrate with PD or in-console schedules (we currently have both mechanisms). Decision needed for private tenants.
- Access control: should only "Policy Admins" set quiet-hours that allow pagers. Add permission check in composer.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Design: create low-fidelity mockups for the three-pane composer (due 2025-02-24) — owner: Marisol
- Eng: draft composer schema and validation rules (RDW-2789 spike) — owner: Darren — due 2025-02-28
- Product: confirm SLO suggestion heuristic and wording with Applied ML (Priya) — due 2025-03-03
- PM: add RDW tickets to backlog and label with priorities (Marisol)

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Think about a "quiet-hours heatmap" that visualizes expected page volume if quiet-hours changed — could be a future Optimize feature.
- Could we auto-suggest channel set based on team membership? e.g., if team has PD integration, suggest Pager + Slack; else Slack + Email.
- Keep the composer URL-stable so customers can embed deep links in runbooks.

Appendix: sample quick flow (user story)
1) Alice (SWE) wants an alert for model-inference p95 > 600ms for route /generate. She clicks "Create Policy" -> selects service and route -> metric p95 > 600ms / 5m -> attaches SLO "Model-p95-99" -> Composer shows "Recommended: severity=high" -> Alice adds Slack channel #model-ops and toggles Pager for severity=critical only -> sets quiet hours for pager 22:00-07:00 PST -> runs "Simulate" -> sees ~40 triggers/week, ~2 pages/week (after throttles) -> saves as "Model p95 policy v1".

Compatibility notes:
- For Dedicated/Private: need to gate simulator access and CSV upload to local data stores; UI should show a note: "Simulation uses anonymized aggregated metrics; for on-premised data upload CSV."

End of doc.
